mainEntity.name: Is this the real Typst compiler?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The editor runs Typst 0.14 compiled to WebAssembly (typst.ts), the same compiler as the Typst command line. A document gives the same pages there if it uses the same fonts and no packages from Typst Universe. It is loaded once (about 11 MB) and then kept by your browser.

mainEntity.name: How do I get a PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Click "Export", choose PDF and click "Download". The PDF comes straight from the Typst compiler, with real text that can be selected and searched.

mainEntity.name: Can I use packages from Typst Universe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not directly: the editor loads nothing from other servers, so #import "@preview/…" reports a problem that names the package. You can add the .typ files of a package to the document in the Pictures tab and import them by file name.

The fonts Typst ships: Libertinus Serif (the default), New Computer Modern and its math font, and DejaVu Sans Mono for code. Add your own .otf or .ttf files to a document and use them with #set text(font: "Name").

Drag or paste a picture into the editor, or add it in the Pictures tab on the right. It is stored with the document in your browser and used by #image("name.png"). CSV, JSON, YAML and .bib files work the same way.

mainEntity.name: Can an AI write in the Typst Editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, any AI - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or the AI in your coding tool. Click "AI Assistant", then "Copy prompt", paste it into your AI and say what it should write. The AI answers with a link; click it and the document appears in your editor. "Undo" takes every change back.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the editor on my own website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Embed it with an iframe and exchange documents with postMessage, or let it send every saved version to your server with a webhook. See Use the editor on your own website for examples.

mainEntity.name: Does the Typst Editor cost anything?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The editor is free, without ads and without sign-up.

page_text:
Write Typst online, with the real compiler

Typst is a markup language for documents such as letters, reports and papers, a newer alternative to LaTeX. The Typst Editor shows your code and the compiled pages side by side. It runs the real Typst compiler in your browser as WebAssembly, and the preview shows the same pages as the PDF - headings, lists, tables, math, figures, footnotes, references and your own #set and #show rules. A click on any text on the page takes you to its place in the code, and you can edit the text right on the page.

Everything runs in your browser. Your documents are kept there, not on our server, and there is no sign-up and no advertising.

What the editor can do

Code with highlighting

Markup, code, math, strings and comments in their own colors, line numbers, lists that continue on Enter, and the compiler's errors with line, column and hint.

The real Typst compiler

Typst 0.14 compiled to WebAssembly runs in a worker next to the editor and compiles a moment after each change - typing stays smooth.

Edit on the page

Click text on the page to change it there; the change goes into the code. A click on math or a picture jumps to its place in the code.

Document settings

Paper, margins, columns, font, size, language, justified text, numbered headings and page numbers - the settings edit the #set rules of your code.

Pictures and data files

Add pictures, CSV, JSON, YAML, bibliographies, fonts and other .typ files to a document and use them with image, csv, json or #import.

Export

A PDF from the compiler with real, selectable text, every page as PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG, or the .typ source with its files as ZIP.

How it works

  1. Start - choose a template under "New", open a .typ file or paste Typst code.
  2. Write - type in the code; the pages on the right follow. Use "Insert" for tables, lists and math.
  3. Export - save a PDF, pictures of the pages or the .typ file.

Use the editor on your own website

Put the editor into your own website with an iframe or in a window of its own. Your page hands it the document, gets every change and every save back, and can let an AI send its results to your server. No sign-up, no key.

Embed the editor on your website →

Frequently asked questions

Is my document uploaded?

No. The editor and the Typst compiler run in your browser and keep your documents there, not on our server. A document goes to a server only if you set up a webhook to your own server, if a website that embeds the editor saves it on its own server, or if another website opens it here with a form (post.php) - our server then passes it straight to your browser without storing it. As on any website, the server logs each visit, and we count page views anonymously - see the privacy policy.

Yes. The editor runs Typst 0.14 compiled to WebAssembly (typst.ts), the same compiler as the Typst command line. A document gives the same pages there if it uses the same fonts and no packages from Typst Universe. It is loaded once (about 11 MB) and then kept by your browser.

How do I get a PDF?

Click "Export", choose PDF and click "Download". The PDF comes straight from the Typst compiler, with real text that can be selected and searched.

Can I use packages from Typst Universe?

Not directly: the editor loads nothing from other servers, so #import "@preview/…" reports a problem that names the package. You can add the .typ files of a package to the document in the Pictures tab and import them by file name.

Which fonts are there?

The fonts Typst ships: Libertinus Serif (the default), New Computer Modern and its math font, and DejaVu Sans Mono for code. Add your own .otf or .ttf files to a document and use them with #set text(font: "Name").

How do I add pictures?

Drag or paste a picture into the editor, or add it in the Pictures tab on the right. It is stored with the document in your browser and used by #image("name.png"). CSV, JSON, YAML and .bib files work the same way.

Yes, any AI - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or the AI in your coding tool. Click "AI Assistant", then "Copy prompt", paste it into your AI and say what it should write. The AI answers with a link; click it and the document appears in your editor. "Undo" takes every change back.

Yes. Embed it with an iframe and exchange documents with postMessage, or let it send every saved version to your server with a webhook. See Use the editor on your own website for examples.

embed.h1: Embed the Typst Editor in your website
embed.intro: For developers: how to put the Typst Editor into your own page - in an iframe, in a window of its own or as a read-only viewer - and how documents, saves and AI results travel between the editor and your server. You need no sign-up and no key from us.
embed.body:
Any https page (and localhost) can embed the editor with an <iframe> and ?embed=1 - no sign-up, no key. Embedded, the editor hides the page text and shows a Save button. There are four ways to get the document in and out.

1. Open a file from a link, save to your server

src= opens a file (your server must allow CORS), webhook= makes "Save" (Ctrl+S) send the document to that address. Add &auto to save after every change.

<iframe src="https://typst.giit.ch/?embed=1&src=https://your-site.com/docs/flyer.typ&webhook=https://your-site.com/save.php"
        allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>

The webhook gets a POST with JSON { editor, event: "save", id, name, content, assets, updated }. A link carries no token (it would end up in server logs and the browser history), so a webhook in the address suits a save address that needs none, for example on localhost or in your intranet. For a public server, hand the webhook over with a token in typsteditor:load (hook: { url, token }) and check it, as this small PHP script does:

<?php
header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://typst.giit.ch');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS');
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'OPTIONS') exit;
if (($_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '') !== 'Bearer SECRET') { http_response_code(403); exit; }
$d = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'), true);
$name = preg_replace('/[^\w\- ]/u', '_', $d['name']);
file_put_contents(__DIR__ . "/docs/$name.typ", $d['content']);
echo '{"ok":true}';

2. Your page holds the document (postMessage)

The editor says typsteditor:ready, your page answers with typsteditor:load, the editor reports typsteditor:loaded, typsteditor:change on real edits and typsteditor:save when the user saves. Your page may send typsteditor:get (the current state) or typsteditor:save (press Save). Saving then goes through your own login and session.

<iframe id="ed" src="https://typst.giit.ch/?embed=1" allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>
<script>
const ed = document.getElementById('ed');
const ORIGIN = 'https://typst.giit.ch';

addEventListener('message', async e => {
  if (e.source !== ed.contentWindow || e.origin !== ORIGIN) return;
  const m = e.data;
  if (m.type === 'typsteditor:ready') {             // the editor is ready: hand it the document
    ed.contentWindow.postMessage({
      type: 'typsteditor:load',
      name: 'Flyer',
      content: await (await fetch('/docs/flyer.typ')).text(),
      assets: { 'logo.png': 'data:image/png;base64,…' }   // optional pictures and data files
    }, ORIGIN);
  }
  if (m.type === 'typsteditor:change') document.title = '● not saved';   // a real edit
  if (m.type === 'typsteditor:save') {              // the user clicked "Save"
    await fetch('/api/save', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ name: m.name, content: m.content, assets: m.assets }) });
    document.title = 'Saved';
  }
});

// A save button on your own page: the answer comes as typsteditor:save
function saveNow() { ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'typsteditor:get' }, ORIGIN); }
</script>

AI Assistant inside your page: it works in the frame too. With allow="clipboard-write" on the iframe, "Copy prompt" uses the clipboard directly (otherwise the editor falls back to the old copy command, or shows the prompt to copy by hand). A link the AI sends cannot reach an editor inside another website, so the editor tells the AI and the user to paste the AI's whole answer into the editor instead - or open the editor in a window of its own.

3. In a window of its own

window.open("https://typst.giit.ch/?embed=window", "typsteditor-17") opens the full editor in its own window and speaks the same messages with window.opener. Links from an AI reach it there. typsteditor:load may also carry context: { host, title, rules } - the AI prompt then says where the document belongs and follows your rules - and hook: { url, token, assets: false }, a webhook for this document only that is never stored. Closing the window with unsaved changes sends typsteditor:closing. typsteditor:pdf asks for the PDF of the page's document and gets it back as a data URI, made by the Typst compiler with real, selectable text.

4. AI through your own server

Hand the editor your own prompt, an address on your site and a key for this editor session. The AI dialog then shows "Connected to" your site, what you tell the AI, and the choice change the current document or make a new one; Copy prompt puts it all together. The AI posts its result with the key to your server, and your page opens it in the editor - a new document opens separately and stays in the user's browser. One key per editor session: it stays valid while the editor is open, and only while it has none the editor asks for it with typsteditor:key-request. The editor never sends the key itself and never stores it; the address must be https on your own host or a subdomain of it.

const key = async () => (await fetch('/api/ai-key.php?doc=17')).json();   // one key per editor session
const k = await key();
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'typsteditor:load', name: 'Flyer', content, ai: {
  label: 'My Site', prompt: 'Keep the [[placeholders]]. Write in German.',
  endpoint: 'https://your-site.com/api/ai-result.php', key: k.key } }, ORIGIN);
// remember the id from typsteditor:loaded and ignore change/save/closing with another id
// only while the editor has no key:
if (m.type === 'typsteditor:key-request') { const k = await key(); ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'typsteditor:ai', key: k.key }, ORIGIN); }
// while the editor is open, tell your server every minute; closing the editor or the page voids the key
setInterval(() => fetch('/api/ai-key.php?alive=' + k.key.slice(0, 8)), 60000);
// your server has a result (polling, SSE …): target is "current" or "new"
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'typsteditor:load', name: 'Flyer', content: draft, from: 'ai', target }, ORIGIN);
<?php // api/ai-key.php - the key of this editor session of the logged-in user (your page calls it)
session_start();                                     // check that the user may edit this document
$key = bin2hex(random_bytes(24));
$_SESSION['ai'][hash('sha256', $key)] = ['doc' => (int)$_GET['doc'], 'seen' => time()];  // or in your database; ?alive= sets seen again
echo json_encode(['key' => $key]);

<?php // api/ai-result.php - the AI posts here (no CORS headers: AIs call it from a server)
$key = preg_replace('/^Bearer\s+/', '', $_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '');
$row = find_key(hash('sha256', $key));               // your database: not voided, seen in the last 3 minutes
if (!$row) { http_response_code(401); exit('{"ok":false,"error":"key not valid"}'); }
$d = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input', false, null, 0, 2000000), true);
save_draft($row['doc'], $d['content'], $d['target'] === 'new' ? 'new' : 'current');   // your page shows it with typsteditor:load
echo '{"ok":true}';

Make keys with at least 128 random bits, store only their hash, bind each to the logged-in user, the document and this editor session, make one per session, keep it valid only while your page reports the session as open, and void it when the editor or the page closes.

Your own AI dialog and answering instructions: with dialog: "page" in ai, a click on AI Assistant sends typsteditor:ai-click with a request id; answer { type: "typsteditor:ai-click", request, handled: true } within 300 ms and show your own dialog - otherwise the editor opens its own. answer: "…" puts your text in place of the "HOW TO ANSWER" part of the copied prompt ("none" leaves the part out, "" brings the editor's part back); the prompt then carries no key. When your server gives no key, answer typsteditor:key-request with { type: "typsteditor:ai", decline: true, message: "…" }: the editor stops waiting at once and shows your message after your host - write it in your page's language. In the prompt the document always stands in a fence longer than any run of backticks in it, marked as data.

The whole protocol is in llms.txt - give it to an AI and it builds the connection for your system. The other giit editors work the same way with their own prefix - editors.giit.ch.

Show a document read-only (viewer)

?viewer=1 shows only the finished document: no code, no tools, nothing can be changed, and nothing is stored in the browser. The document comes from a link (#b64=, ?src=), from your page with typsteditor:load, or by POST as a normal form to post.php: the field content as text or b64 as base64, optionally name, at most 20 MB of text.

<form method="post" action="https://typst.giit.ch/post.php?viewer=1" target="_blank">
  <input type="hidden" name="name" value="Report">
  <input type="hidden" name="b64" value="…">
  <button>Open</button>
</form>

Without viewer=1 the document opens in the normal editor. Either way it is kept in memory only: it is not stored on the server and does not join "My documents". Opened directly, the viewer says that the content comes from a third party.

Templates with placeholders

When your server fills placeholders into the Typst code before it is used, add template=mustache for {{name}}, {{#name}} … {{/name}} and {{^name}} … {{/name}}, or template=angle for <<name>> and <<?name>> … <</?name>>. The list of problems reads every tag as one placeholder and reports a section left open, a stray end tag, an end tag in the wrong order and a tag with an unknown sign; the code shows the tags as written. A placeholder stands in text, strings and comments; in code it goes into a string ("{{name}}").

Send your placeholders with examples and example pictures, and the pages show the document filled with them: sections by their example state, a list once per example row, pictures from assets (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 20 and 40 MB). Each example is written for its place - escaped in markup, as a string in math and code. A placeholder without an example shows its label in brackets, such as [Name]. The switch Template in the bar of the pages shows the tags as text and compiles also with raw tags, Examples brings the examples back; the box Placeholders below the code puts a tag at the cursor. Examples are shown as text, stay in memory only and never reach your page: saving, change, get, the webhook, the .typ and the ZIP carry the template as written, and the pictures of the pages (PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG) show the template view; the PDF and print follow the view shown, and print names it in its title. A picture whose file name holds a placeholder shows a placeholder picture in the template view.

frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'typsteditor:template',
  placeholders: [
    { name: 'name', kind: 'value', label: 'Name', example: 'John Doe' },
    { name: 'logo', kind: 'image', label: 'Logo', image: 'logo.png' },
    { name: 'hasNote', kind: 'section', label: 'With a note', shown: true },
    { name: 'items', kind: 'list', label: 'Items',
      fields: [ { name: 'label', label: 'Item' }, { name: 'quantity', label: 'Quantity' } ],
      rows: [ { label: 'Chair', quantity: '2' }, { label: 'Table', quantity: '1' } ] } ],
  assets: { 'logo.png': 'data:image/png;base64,…' } }, ORIGIN);
// or the same object as the field template of typsteditor:load; { type: 'typsteditor:template', clear: true } ends it
<iframe src="https://typst.giit.ch/?embed=1&template=mustache" allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>
